title: CSS Containment & Rendering Pipelines
description: Archived challenge exploring browser layout boundaries, content-visibility, and paint isolation.
author: Qodlume Editorial

questions.prompt: Which CSS property allows the browser to skip rendering work (layout and paint) for off-screen elements until they approach the viewport?
questions.explanation: content-visibility: auto instructs the user agent to skip layout, style, and paint work for off-screen subtrees while contain-intrinsic-size provides a placeholder geometry to avoid scrollbar jitter.

questions.prompt: What does 'contain: layout' guarantee to the browser layout engine?

options.text: Nothing outside the element affects its internal layout, and nothing inside affects the layout of outside elements.
The element cannot use Flexbox or CSS Grid.
Child elements cannot inherit font or color properties.
The element is automatically promoted to a GPU WebGL context.

questions.explanation: Layout containment establishes an independent formatting context boundary so that internal layout mutations do not require dirtying or reflowing the rest of the document tree.
